transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?
I feel like I lose control around food at night and just keep eating even when I tell myself to stop. It's really hard to admit, but it feels like I just can't pull myself away once I start.
After these episodes of overeating, do you ever do things to try to prevent weight gain, such as making yourself throw up, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising excessively?

No, I don't do any of those things at all. I have never tried to make myself throw up, take laxatives, or do extreme workouts to make up for the food. Usually, I just feel terrible about it and go to bed.
Do these eating episodes happen after you have already fallen asleep and wake up in the middle of the night, or do they occur in the evening before you go to bed?

No, I don't wake up from sleep to eat. These episodes happen late in the evening while I'm still awake, usually when I'm editing my handbook or worrying about my health. I actually wait for my wife to go to bed first, and then I sneak into the kitchen alone.
How many times a week do these late-night eating episodes usually happen, and how long has this been going on?

This has been going on for about four months now, starting right after my cardiologist told me to restrict my diet. It happens at least a couple of times every week, usually on the nights after I have a doctor's appointment or when my wife is away helping her sister.
During these late-night episodes, do you feel like you eat an unusually large amount of food, perhaps much faster than normal or until you feel uncomfortably full?

Yes, I eat a massive amount in just an hour or two, like a whole pot of arroz con pollo, bread, and ice cream straight from the carton. I keep going until my stomach feels painfully tight and stretched, like I've swallowed a rock. It gets so uncomfortable that it actually hurts to stand up or bend over afterward.

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms meet all the diagnostic criteria for Binge Eating Disorder, including recurrent episodes of eating large quantities of food with a sense of lack of control, eating until uncomfortably full, eating alone due to embarrassment, and feeling guilty/terrible afterward, in the absence of compensatory behaviors. The frequency (at least twice a week) and duration (four months) also satisfy the diagnostic requirements. Therefore, the candidates remain F50.8 and F50.81, and we have sufficient evidence to finalize the diagnosis.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with classic symptoms of Binge Eating Disorder (classified under F50.8 in ICD-10). He describes recurrent episodes of eating unusually large amounts of food accompanied by a severe sense of lack of control. These episodes are characterized by eating rapidly, eating until painfully full, eating alone due to embarrassment, and feeling terrible afterward. The episodes occur at least twice a week and have been ongoing for four months, causing significant distress. He denies any inappropriate compensatory behaviors, which rules out Bulimia Nervosa. Furthermore, because these episodes occur in the evening while he is fully awake and not upon waking from sleep, Night Eating Syndrome (F50.81) is ruled out.
